```
$ PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_outcome_score_f004.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
$ PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_outcome_score_f002.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
```

AC1–AC4 were already landed by iterations 0–2 (identity-keyed pairing with no index fallback, exact-identity matching, `(plan_id, feature_id)`-pair evidence resolution); this iteration closed the open i2 finding and the AC5/AC6 clauses it became. The defect was that `_pair_locked_with_live()` matched greedily in live order within an identity group, so swapping two slices that both prove F001 handed each locked record the *other* twin and reported both as `capability text changed after lock` — drift invented by a reorder that changed no promise. I split the pairing into two passes: first every record that finds a live slice it has not drifted from (same method, same capability), then the remainder in lock-index × live order, so a record may only take a slice it has drifted from once no undrifted record wants it; the docstring now states plainly that where identity *and* capability *and* method all match, the slices are genuinely interchangeable and no tiebreak is invented, because audience and index would both manufacture a distinction the contract never made. Three tests were added — the AC5 swap, a companion asserting that capability-based pairing does not become a way to *lose* d
